{"self_assessment": "Impact: I picked the fish early (a single loop with a forked tail) and sketched it on the pad within the first minute, so the table had a plan and a shared reference from the start. I laid the top curve of the body and later the bridge joining the lower lobe to the body. At the push, the body, top curve and lower lobe were connected to the start. I can't say yet whether the judge recognized the fish. About 131 of the 190 standing dominoes were connected, so some leftover pale pieces on the right won't fall. I hope they don't muddy the outline. I didn't confirm the end result myself.

Execution: My own pieces got done, but not as cleanly as they could have been. The lobe bridge took until about 9:15, close to the deadline, and I stayed off the start junction while Tom fixed it. I told Leo not to lift a pale line, and he said it was just a leftover. We cleared that up, but I should have checked what it was before speaking. I didn't take part in clearing the stray right-hand loop, and I didn't inspect the whole picture before the push. I'm trusting teammates' checks that the lobe is dark all the way to the tail edge.

Collaboration: I assigned each person a stroke, thanked people when they took one, and kept the table updated on what I was doing and where. I stayed off Tom's junction and Priya's lobe to avoid bumps, and I told people to hold back when I had a piece in hand. When Leo offered help, I said no. That was fine for the bridge, but I could have accepted a hand sooner.

Leadership: I set the concept, split the work and kept the group aligned around one sketch. I also set a fallback (bridge the body from the other side if it was still pale with two minutes left). Next time I'd assign someone to check the whole run against the start before the final minutes, and I'd flag the stray pieces earlier."}
